title: GPU Fleet Ops Standup - capacity & regional status (2026-03-09)
linked_artifacts: Confluence: GPU Fleet Capacity Runbook (page id: 4521)
summary: Weekly sync focused on short-term capacity adjustments for upcoming benchmark week, regional imbalance remediation, and the H100 migration pilot timeline. Quick review of ongoing evacuation test outcomes and action items for reducing cold-start latency in eu-west-1.
updates: 1) Fleet utilization: global GPU utilization averaged 68% last 7 days; peak sustained windows hit 92% in us-west-2 during load tests. 2) Instance mix: A100 pool (reserved) at 1,120 devices, H100 pool (spot/dedicated pilot) expanded to 240 devices in us-west-2 for pilot traffic. 3) Regional notes: eu-west-1 is experiencing higher queue times (~420ms head-of-line) due to imbalance of small-instance backing capacity; ap-northeast-1 stable but constrained for burst capacity. 4) Storage/IO: observed intermittent NVMe overheating events on 4 hosts (INFRA-421), currently remediated with firmware update and thermal throttling policy. 5) Network: inter-region egress spikes from us-east-1 during snapshot windows causing small increase in token latency; Leah to propose staggered snapshot schedule. 6) Cost: finance flagged >15% month-over-month GPU spot spend increase tied to expanded H100 pilot hours. Dana requested CAPPLAN-58 breakdown for next finance review.
metrics:
- Global 7d avg GPU utilization: 68%
- 7d p95 request latency (token): 120ms hosted, 160ms in private edges
- Queue time p95 (eu-west-1): 420ms; target <200ms
- Cold start rate (on-demand kernel init): 3.8% of requests; target <1%
- Reserved vs spot usage: 72% reserved, 28% spot (by GPU-hours)
- Evacuation test recovery time (node drain -> capacity recovery): 7m 12s average
- Failed job rate last 48h: 0.6% (mostly transient OOM during long-seq tests)
discussion_notes:
- H100 pilot: Samir reported early quality gains for long-context models; however the thermal profile requires tuning. Decision to keep pilot in us-west-2 for one more week, then expand to a small pool in eu-west-1 if thermal fixes pass. (Action: Samir + Diego to run thermal regression tests and update PR #981).
- eu-west-1 queue spike root-cause: discovered that autoscale policy for small-instance pool has a 5-min cooldown that is too long for bursty traffic. Short-term mitigation: reduce cooldown to 60s for the small-instance autoscaler. (Action: Avery to rollout change to staging and monitor).
- Evacuation test on 2026-03-07: drained 18 hosts in us-west-2; observed two 1m spikes in token latency while KV-cache warmed. We agreed to add a background warmup task that preloads common prefixes during drain. (Action: Priya to file runbook update & Samir to prototype warmup job).
- Snapshot scheduling: Leah proposed distributed snapshot windows to smooth inter-region egress. Agreed to pilot staggering across regions with 15m offsets during off-peak hours. (Action: Leah).
- Cost vs performance trade: Dana asked for a proposal to cap H100 spot hours for next month to stay within budget; Samir will prepare CAPPLAN-58 addendum with three scenarios (conservative/moderate/aggressive).
decisions:
- Keep H100 pilot in us-west-2 for one additional week.
- Reduce small-instance autoscaler cooldown from 5m to 60s in eu-west-1 (staging first).
- Implement background KV warmup during node drains as high-priority engineering task.
- Stagger snapshot windows by region with 15-minute offsets for two-week trial.
- Finance limit: temporary cap on H100 spot expansion until CAPPLAN-58 is approved.
action_items:
- Samir + Diego: run full thermal regression on H100 hosts and post results to PR #981; due 2026-03-12.
- Avery: deploy autoscaler cooldown change to staging eu-west-1 and collect queue-time metrics; due 2026-03-10.
- Priya: update evacuation runbook with KV warmup steps and lead warmup implementation prioritization; due 2026-03-13.
- Leah: design staggered snapshot schedule and rollout plan; coordinate with storage team; due 2026-03-14.
- Dana: finalize temporary budget cap parameters and circulate to infra leads; due 2026-03-11.
- Samir: CAPPLAN-58 addendum with H100 scenarios; due 2026-03-16.
- Avery: follow up on INFRA-421 NVMe hosts and confirm stable telemetry; ongoing, update in next standup.
risks_and_blockers:
- Thermal limits on new H100 hosts could delay expansion to eu-west-1. Workaround: keep pilot small and tune BIOS/firmware.
- Autoscaler policy change could cause over-provisioning if cooldown too short; mitigation: staging rollout + rate limit.
- Background warmup job could add extra load during drains; need to cap concurrency and prioritize low-cost prefix sets.
- Finance cap may block necessary burst capacity for benchmark week; coordinate to allow scheduled exempted windows for customer-critical runs.
notes_and_misc:
- Quick wins: enable NVMe firmware auto-update on maintenance window to avoid manual patch cycles.
- Reminder: upcoming benchmark week (2026-03-16) — product will run multi-model stress tests; ensure extra buffer of 8% reserved capacity in primary regions.
- Observability: add a panel showing cold-start kernel-init rate by region (requested by Avery).
- Good shoutout: SRE on-call handled the 03/07 drain smoothly; reduced incident blast radius and kept SLOs within threshold.
- Open question: do we want to start tagging H100 hosts with a capability label to enable smarter routing? Tony suggested capability labels in internal RFC.
